1000361.etyen:
Internationalism, based on New Latin Bosnia, ultimately from Serbo-Croatian Bȍsna, the name of the historical region. The region is named after the river Bȍsna. The deeper origin of the river name is uncertain; a pre-Slavic origin has traditionally been proposed, while a Slavic origin has also been argued.
Compare Danish Bosnien, Swedish Bosnien, German Bosnien, Dutch Bosnië, French Bosnie and English Bosnia.

1004713.etyen:
From a Norwegian place-name compound of Old Norse sær (“sea”) and bœr (“farm, settlement”), literally “sea farm” or “farm by the sea”. The first element corresponds semantically to modern sjø (“sea, lake”). The second element bœr is related to búa (“to dwell, live”).
Compare similarly formed Danish Sæby and Swedish Sjöbo (“place names”).
